title: "Environment Variables Reference"

# Environment Variables

SPARMVET_VIZ uses four environment variables to configure the deployment context at launch. They are the only supported mechanism for injecting deployment-specific configuration into the app without modifying files.

All four are read by `app/src/bootloader.py` at startup. The app prints which profile and app features it loaded — check the terminal output to verify:

```
[Bootloader] Profile resolved at level N (<source>): /absolute/path/to/profile.yaml
[Bootloader] App features: <id> → /absolute/path/to/config/ui/templates/<id>_template.yaml
```

---

## Reference table

| Variable | Required? | Default | Set by | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SPARMVET_PROFILE` | No | Falls through 4-level chain | Galaxy XML, IRIDA container, Docker Compose, systemd | **Absolute path** to a deployment profile YAML. When set, skips all other resolution levels. Raises `FileNotFoundError` immediately if the path does not exist. |
| `SPARMVET_APP_FEATURES` | Conditionally | `default_app_features` in profile | Developer, Galaxy XML, Docker Compose | **Path to an app features config YAML file**, or legacy shortname. Controls which UI features are visible and enabled. See [App features path resolution](#app features coupling) below. |
| `SPARMVET_CONNECTOR` | No | `"local"` | Legacy / backward compat | Connector type; used only as a fallback key for the level-4 dev profile path (`config/deployment/<connector>/local_profile.yaml`). In practice always `"local"` — the profile's `deployment_type` field is the canonical place to declare the connector now. |
| `SPARMVET_IRIDA_TOKEN` | Only for IRIDA deployments | none — raises `AuthenticationError` if unset | IRIDA platform at container launch | OAuth2 bearer token for `IridaConnector`. **Never store in any file** — IRIDA injects this at runtime only. |

---

## Deployment profile resolution chain

`SPARMVET_PROFILE` participates in a 4-level priority chain. The first match wins:

```
1. SPARMVET_PROFILE env var        → /path/to/profile.yaml   (Galaxy, IRIDA, Docker, systemd)
2. ~/.sparmvet/profile.yaml         → user-level, local PC
3. /etc/sparmvet/profile.yaml       → system-level, institutional server
4. config/deployment/local/local_profile.yaml  → developer repo fallback
```

In practice:

- **Local developer**: level 4 (repo fallback) — no setup needed.
- **Scientist on their own machine**: place `~/.sparmvet/profile.yaml` once — level 2, no env var needed.
- **Galaxy tool**: Galaxy XML wrapper sets `SPARMVET_PROFILE` in `<environment_variables>` — level 1.
- **IRIDA**: IRIDA plugin sets `SPARMVET_PROFILE` + `SPARMVET_IRIDA_TOKEN` — level 1.
- **Docker Compose / server**: `SPARMVET_PROFILE` set in the service definition — level 1.

---

## App features resolution order

`SPARMVET_APP_FEATURES` participates in a 3-level priority chain:

```
1. app features= kwarg to Bootloader()      → programmatic (used in tests only)
2. SPARMVET_APP_FEATURES env var            → developer launch / CI
3. default_app_features in deployment profile → production deployments (Galaxy, IRIDA)
```

If none of the three is set, the app raises `ValueError` at startup and refuses to start.

**Production deployments** (Galaxy, IRIDA) should set `default_app_features` in the profile rather than using the env var — that way the app features is bundled with the profile and no additional configuration is needed at launch.

**CI / Playwright tests** must set `SPARMVET_APP_FEATURES=qa` — the `qa` app features has all flags `true` and `ghost_save: false` for determinism.

---

## App features path resolution {#app features coupling}

`SPARMVET_APP_FEATURES` accepts either a **file path** (recommended) or a **legacy shortname**:

| Value | How resolved |
|---|---|
| `/absolute/path/to/my_app_features.yaml` | Loaded directly from that path |
| `config/ui/templates/developer_template.yaml` | Loaded from that relative path |
| `developer` | Shortname → `config/ui/templates/developer_template.yaml` (backward compat) |

The app features config file can be placed **anywhere** — there is no filename convention requirement. The file's `display_name` field is used in the UI header; the `app_features_id` field is an internal identifier within the file. Neither needs to match the filename.

**To create and use a custom app features:**

```bash
# 1. Copy any existing template as a starting point
cp config/ui/templates/project-independent_template.yaml /my/configs/amr_pipeline_app_features.yaml

# 2. Edit display_name, app_features_id, and feature flags in the new file
# 3. Launch with the path
SPARMVET_APP_FEATURES=/my/configs/amr_pipeline_app_features.yaml \
  ./.venv/bin/python -m shiny run app/src/main.py --port 8001
```

**For Galaxy / Docker / IRIDA:** set `SPARMVET_APP_FEATURES` to the absolute path of the app features file in the container image. Each pipeline wrapper can point to a different file:

```xml
<!-- Galaxy XML wrapper — AMR pipeline -->
<environment_variable name="SPARMVET_PROFILE">/profiles/amr_profile.yaml</environment_variable>
<environment_variable name="SPARMVET_APP_FEATURES">/profiles/amr_persona.yaml</environment_variable>

<!-- Galaxy XML wrapper — Plasmid pipeline -->
<environment_variable name="SPARMVET_PROFILE">/profiles/plasmid_profile.yaml</environment_variable>
<environment_variable name="SPARMVET_APP_FEATURES">/profiles/plasmid_persona.yaml</environment_variable>
```

Alternatively, embed `default_app_features` in each deployment profile (pointing to a path) so that only `SPARMVET_PROFILE` needs to be set at launch:

```yaml
# /profiles/amr_profile.yaml
default_app_features: /profiles/amr_persona.yaml
```

---

## Quick reference — developer launch commands

```bash
export PYTHONPATH=$PYTHONPATH:.

# Using shortnames (backward compat — resolves to config/ui/templates/<id>_template.yaml)
SPARMVET_APP_FEATURES=developer            ./.venv/bin/python -m shiny run app/src/main.py --port 8001
SPARMVET_APP_FEATURES=project-independent  ./.venv/bin/python -m shiny run app/src/main.py --port 8001
SPARMVET_APP_FEATURES=pipeline-static      ./.venv/bin/python -m shiny run app/src/main.py --port 8001

# Using a file path (recommended for custom/production app features files)
SPARMVET_APP_FEATURES=/my/configs/amr_app_features.yaml \
  ./.venv/bin/python -m shiny run app/src/main.py --port 8001

# CI / Playwright smoke tests: all flags on, ghost_save off
SPARMVET_APP_FEATURES=qa ./.venv/bin/python -m pytest app/tests/test_shiny_smoke.py -v

# Explicit profile + app features (both as paths — fully portable)
SPARMVET_PROFILE=/path/to/my_profile.yaml \
SPARMVET_APP_FEATURES=/path/to/my_app_features.yaml \
  ./.venv/bin/python -m shiny run app/src/main.py --port 8001
```

## Deployment profile fields (not env vars)

The following fields are set inside the deployment profile YAML, not as environment variables. They are documented here for discoverability.

### `prefer_discovery`

```yaml
prefer_discovery: true    # default: false (absent)
```

When `true`, the orchestrator strips `source` blocks from manifest schema entries before ingest. The ingestor discovers data files in `raw_data_dir` by schema ID name (`*{schema_id}*.tsv`) instead of reading an explicit path.

Use this on any deployment profile that simulates or implements production connector delivery (pipeline delivers data to `raw_data_dir`). Do NOT set on the local dev fallback profile — developers rely on `source.path` to run manifests against arbitrary test data.

The `source.path` field in manifest schema entries is a development shortcut only. It is never used when `prefer_discovery: true`, and is never used in production (Galaxy, IRIDA) regardless of this flag.

See `docs/workflows/connector.qmd` for the full connector lifecycle and per-profile guidance.
